free_tier.stated: No free test. The provider's own FAQ states outright that there is no free testing for cloud servers and that the minimum way to evaluate one is to top up RUB 100 and run it hourly; a separate grant of up to RUB 30,000 exists but only for legal entities and sole proprietors.

per_object_cap.notes: The primary constraint is the virtual machine hardware specification.

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine or an account, not stored bytes
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the running process, not a stored object

chaining: The 3 TB of pooled free egress across all projects is the durable item here, and it composes with any Russian-hosted workload; the compute itself has no free lane at all.

limits.value: There is no free lane for an individual at all: the RUB 30,000 grant is restricted to legal entities and individual entrepreneurs, and everything else starts at a RUB 100 balance.

evidence.proved: the FAQ on the cloud server page states, in Russian, that Selectel has no free testing, and that to evaluate a server it is enough to top the balance up by the minimum amount of RUB 100; the page then explains that a 2 vCPU and 4 GB server can be judged that way

the grant page states, in Russian, that registering in the control panel yields a grant of up to RUB 30,000 in bonuses for testing cloud services over one month, and that the offer is available to legal entities and individual entrepreneurs

the billing documentation states, in Russian, that pay-as-you-go billing deducts hourly for the previous hour of resources plus external traffic consumed above the free allowance of 3 TB across all projects of the account

notes: Selectel offers dedicated enterprise cloud infrastructure in Russia. Promotional startup grants of up to RUB 30,000 are restricted to verified corporate legal entities.
